name_en: Feng Huang Tuo Cha (Nanjian Phoenix Tuo)
processing: Pu-erh pressed into a bowl-shaped tuo by the Nanjian Tulin factory. The ripe version is wet-piled before steaming and pressing; the factory also makes raw tuos, so check the wrapper.
harvest_season: No specific picking is advertised; tuos are sold by recipe and production year.
appearance_dry: A firm, dark brown bowl-shaped tuo in the ripe version.
appearance_liquor: Dark red-brown, as is typical of ripe pu-erh.
appearance_wet: Dark brown leaf and fragments, soft after steeping.
taste_profile: As is typical of ripe factory tuos, an earthy, woody, smooth cup with little bitterness; the exact character depends on the recipe.

brewing.notes: Pry apart from the hollow side and rinse once or twice. Hard-pressed tuos open slowly, so judge it from the third steep on.

vintage_note: Sold by production year and recipe number, such as 8502 for a 2020 ripe tuo. As with other factory shu, it is drunk young or after several years of rest. Because raw and ripe share the brand, confirm which you are buying.
description:
Feng huang means phoenix, and this is the tuo of the Nanjian factory in Dali prefecture, sold under the Tulin brand. Its factory is younger than Xiaguan and lies in the same prefecture.

The ripe version follows the usual route: wet-piled leaf, steamed and pressed into a small bowl. The factory also works with numbered recipes, and it makes raw tea too, so the phoenix on a wrapper does not by itself tell you which kind of tea is inside.

Expect the comfortable profile of factory shu: earth, wood and smooth sweetness. Use very hot water, rinse well and allow a few steeps for the tuo to open before judging it.

Read the wrapper for recipe, year and raw or ripe. These tuos are generally everyday tea, and that is the right way to approach them: a good way of trying a Dali factory style without much outlay.
history:
The Nanjian county tea factory was set up in 1985 and created the Tulin phoenix tuo that year, by the company's own account.

The Tulin trademark followed in 1986 or 1987, depending on the account. The business became a county tea company in 1991, a shareholding cooperative in 1997 and Yunnan Tulin Tea Co. in 2007. Most of this record comes from the company and its sellers.
